prompts: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: four workout animation keyframes on one square 2×2 atlas. Draw four equally sized square cells in a precise two-by-two grid with no panel lines, labels or text. Each cell has the same pure white background, same detailed clean anime fitness-game shading, and the same adult male athlete with short slightly spiky black hair, athletic realistic proportions, fitted red sleeveless gym shirt, black shorts, and red trainers. Place the athlete on one low-profile charcoal workout mat, with the mat in exactly the same place and orientation in every cell. Leave matching margins on every side with full body and mat visible. Side Plank Rotation (thread the needle). Stationary camera, front three-quarter view, athlete's head at left and feet at right in all four panels. The bottom forearm and elbow stay planted on the same mark of the mat beneath the bottom shoulder. The legs remain straight, feet stacked at the same marks, and hips stay lifted. The upper arm is a single continuous limb. Top left: chest open toward the viewer, top hand reaching vertically upward. Top right: top hand arcs forward in front of the ribs and chest starts rotating toward the mat. Bottom left: top hand reaches beneath the rib cage, chest turned partly toward the floor, supporting arm remains completely steady. Bottom right: intermediate opening pose, with the SAME moving arm emerging from under the ribs and reaching out, ready to return to the first panel. Make the top hand path and turning rib cage easy to read. Only two arms total. Never draw a faint old position, a duplicated arm, a floating hand, or a different view. Keep the supporting elbow, legs, shoes and mat identical. Use clearly rendered muscles and controlled, mechanically readable training poses. Match scale, joint proportions, floor, hair, lighting, and outline style through all four cells. No graphic overlays.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: four workout animation keyframes on one square 2×2 atlas. Draw four equally sized square cells in a precise two-by-two grid with no panel lines, labels or text. Each cell has the same pure white background, same detailed clean anime fitness-game shading, and the same adult male athlete with short slightly spiky black hair, athletic realistic proportions, fitted red sleeveless gym shirt, black shorts, and red trainers. Place the athlete on one low-profile charcoal workout mat, with the mat in exactly the same place and orientation in every cell. Leave matching margins on every side with full body and mat visible. Alternating Bicycle Crunch. Use the same elevated foot-end three-quarter camera for all four panels, looking down along a diagonal so both legs are fully visible and the head is left of the feet. The athlete's hips remain on the same mark on the mat. Both hands rest lightly behind the ears with elbows open. The shoulder blade lifts and rib cage turns as the opposite leg bends. Top left: centered transition with both knees bent and both legs clearly separate. Top right: RIGHT knee moves in toward LEFT elbow as LEFT leg extends low in the air. Bottom left: centered crossing transition with both legs bent at distinct depths and shoulders neutral. Bottom right: LEFT knee moves in toward RIGHT elbow as RIGHT leg extends low in the air. Clearly show that the working leg alternates. Show two distinct complete legs with exactly two knees and two red shoes in each pose. Keep the hips on the mat and framing identical, no camera swivel. Do not reuse the same working leg in both endpoint panels. No ghost limbs, overlapped silhouettes that hide a knee, yanking at the neck, or stretched torso. Use clearly rendered muscles and controlled, mechanically readable training poses. Match scale, joint proportions, floor, hair, lighting, and outline style through all four cells. No graphic overlays.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the 2×2 exercise sprite sheet to edit. Preserve the exact first three panels, same character, white background, black mat with identical diagonal vanishing lines, margins, cell divisions, pixel scale, light and locked camera. Edit only the athlete inside the BOTTOM RIGHT panel. The existing TOP RIGHT panel correctly shows the near leg (the leg closest to the camera at the lower-left side of the hips) bent up and the far leg extended. The new BOTTOM RIGHT must be its actual opposite action, seen from the EXACT SAME camera, not a mirror of the camera. In the bottom right, the closest thigh follows the lower foreground edge of the body and its knee stays low and STRAIGHT, with that near shin extended diagonally toward the bottom right corner close over the lower edge of the mat. The OTHER thigh, emerging from the far, upper edge of the pelvis on the far side of the body, flexes up and in toward the ribs, its knee visibly bent close to the NEAR elbow. That far knee appears behind and to the right of the near elbow in the picture; its red shoe is lifted higher than the red shoe of the extended near leg. The shoulder closest to the viewer curls across the chest toward that far knee, while the far elbow stays open. Both hands remain at the ears. Render exactly two continuous legs, two knees, two red shoes and two arms. This is an opposite elbow to knee Bicycle Crunch switch, not a camera or viewpoint change. Keep the location of the pelvis on the mat and the mat corners identical. No overlays, arrows, lettering, ghost limbs, or other changes.
